worked_solution:
If $x=0$ is a regular singular point of a second-order homogeneous linear differential equation, then the method of Frobenius states that there is at least one solution of the form

$$
y={x}^{\lambda }{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }{a}_{n}{x}^{n},
$$

where $\lambda $ and ${a}_{n}$ for $n=0,1,2,…$ are constants.

Substituting this solution and its derivatives into the ODE, collecting like terms, and setting coefficients equal to zero, we obtain:

- the indicial equation from the coefficients of the $n=0$ term for arbitrary ${a}_{0},$ and

- a recurrence formula from the coefficients of the $n\ge 1$ terms.

We are given the three terms of the ODE as power series with the $n=0$ term isolated in each.

$$
\begin{aligned}3{x}^{2}{y}^{″} & =3({\lambda }^{2}-\lambda ){a}_{0}{x}^{\lambda }+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }3((\lambda +n)^{2}-(\lambda +n)){a}_{n}{x}^{\lambda +n}, \\ 2x(x+4){y}^{′} & =8\lambda {a}_{0}{x}^{\lambda }+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }[2(\lambda +n-1){a}_{n-1}+8(\lambda +n){a}_{n}]{x}^{\lambda +n}, \\ -12y & =-12{a}_{0}{x}^{\lambda }-{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }12{a}_{n}{x}^{\lambda +n}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we continue from this point.

**Step 1**: Consolidate all the series into a single series that is equal to $0.$

Collecting the terms for $n=0,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}3({\lambda }^{2}-\lambda ){a}_{0}{x}^{\lambda }+8\lambda {a}_{0}{x}^{\lambda }-12{a}_{0}{x}^{\lambda } & = \\ (3{\lambda }^{2}-3\lambda +8\lambda -12){a}_{0}{x}^{\lambda } & = \\ (3{\lambda }^{2}+5\lambda -12){a}_{0}{x}^{\lambda }. & \end{aligned}
$$

Similarly, collecting terms for $n\ge 1,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }[3((\lambda +n)^{2}-(\lambda +n)){a}_{n}+2(\lambda +n-1){a}_{n-1}+8(\lambda +n){a}_{n}-12{a}_{n}]{x}^{\lambda +n} & = \\ {x}^{\lambda }{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }[3(\lambda +n)^{2}{a}_{n}+5(\lambda +n){a}_{n}-12{a}_{n}+2(\lambda +n-1){a}_{n-1}]{x}^{n} & = \\ {x}^{\lambda }{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }[(3(\lambda +n)^{2}+5(\lambda +n)-12){a}_{n}+2(\lambda +n-1){a}_{n-1}]{x}^{n} & .\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,(3{\lambda }^{2}+5\lambda -12){a}_{0}{x}^{\lambda }+{x}^{\lambda }{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }[(3(\lambda +n)^{2}+5(\lambda +n)-12){a}_{n}+2(\lambda +n-1){a}_{n-1}]{x}^{n} & =0 \\ \,\,\,\,(3{\lambda }^{2}+5\lambda -12){a}_{0}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }[(3(\lambda +n)^{2}+5(\lambda +n)-12){a}_{n}+2(\lambda +n-1){a}_{n-1}]{x}^{n} & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 2**:  Set the coefficients of the series equal to $0.$

Setting the coefficients of the $n=0$ term equal to $0$ with arbitrary ${a}_{0}\ne 0,$ we obtain the indicial equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}(3{\lambda }^{2}+5\lambda -12){a}_{0} & =0 \\ (3\lambda -4)(\lambda +3) & =0 \\ \lambda  & =-3,\frac{4}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Since we're interested in $\lambda \in (1,2),$ we take $\lambda =\frac{4}{3}.$

Similarly, setting the coefficients of ${x}^{n}$ for $n\ge 1$ equal to $0,$ we obtain the following recurrence relation:

$$
\begin{aligned}(3(\lambda +n)^{2}+5(\lambda +n)-12){a}_{n}+2(\lambda +n-1){a}_{n-1} & =0 \\ (3(\lambda +n)-4)((\lambda +n)+3){a}_{n} & =-2(\lambda +n-1){a}_{n-1}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute $\lambda =\frac{4}{3}$ into the above and solve for ${a}_{n}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(3(\frac{4}{3}+n)-4)((\frac{4}{3}+n)+3){a}_{n} & =-2(\frac{4}{3}+n-1){a}_{n-1} \\ 3n(n+\frac{13}{3}){a}_{n} & =-2(n+\frac{1}{3}){a}_{n-1} \\ n(3n+13){a}_{n} & =-\frac{2}{3}(3n+1){a}_{n-1} \\ {a}_{n} & =\frac{2(-3n-1)}{3n(3n+13)}\,{a}_{n-1}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $f(n)=3n(3n+13).$

If x=0 is a regular singular point of a second-order homogeneous linear differential equation, then the method of Frobenius states that there is at least one solution of the form y=xλ∑n=0∞anxn, where λ and an for n=0,1,2,… are constants.

Substituting this solution and its derivatives into the ODE, collecting like terms, and setting coefficients equal to zero, we obtain:

  • the indicial equation from the coefficients of the n=0 term for arbitrary a0, and

  • a recurrence formula from the coefficients of the n≥1 terms.

We are given the three terms of the ODE as power series with the n=0 term isolated in each.

3x2y″=3(λ2−λ)a0xλ+∑n=1∞3((λ+n)2−(λ+n))anxλ+n,2x(x+4)y′=8λa0xλ+∑n=1∞[2(λ+n−1)an−1+8(λ+n)an]xλ+n,−12y=−12a0xλ−∑n=1∞12anxλ+n.

Now, we continue from this point.

Step 1: Consolidate all the series into a single series that is equal to 0.

Collecting the terms for n=0, we have

3(λ2−λ)a0xλ+8λa0xλ−12a0xλ=(3λ2−3λ+8λ−12)a0xλ=(3λ2+5λ−12)a0xλ.

Similarly, collecting terms for n≥1, we have

∑n=1∞[3((λ+n)2−(λ+n))an+2(λ+n−1)an−1+8(λ+n)an−12an]xλ+n=xλ∑n=1∞[3(λ+n)2an+5(λ+n)an−12an+2(λ+n−1)an−1]xn=xλ∑n=1∞[(3(λ+n)2+5(λ+n)−12)an+2(λ+n−1)an−1]xn.

Therefore, we obtain

(3λ2+5λ−12)a0xλ+xλ∑n=1∞[(3(λ+n)2+5(λ+n)−12)an+2(λ+n−1)an−1]xn=0(3λ2+5λ−12)a0+∑n=1∞[(3(λ+n)2+5(λ+n)−12)an+2(λ+n−1)an−1]xn=0.

Step 2: Set the coefficients of the series equal to 0.

Setting the coefficients of the n=0 term equal to 0 with arbitrary a0≠0, we obtain the indicial equation:

(3λ2+5λ−12)a0=0(3λ−4)(λ+3)=0λ=−3,43

Since we're interested in λ∈(1,2), we take λ=43.

Similarly, setting the coefficients of xn for n≥1 equal to 0, we obtain the following recurrence relation:

(3(λ+n)2+5(λ+n)−12)an+2(λ+n−1)an−1=0(3(λ+n)−4)((λ+n)+3)an=−2(λ+n−1)an−1

Finally, we substitute λ=43 into the above and solve for an:

(3(43+n)−4)((43+n)+3)an=−2(43+n−1)an−13n(n+133)an=−2(n+13)an−1n(3n+13)an=−23(3n+1)an−1an=2(−3n−1)3n(3n+13)an−1

Therefore, f(n)=3n(3n+13).
